gap: No result ChatGPT got states that RTINGS measured only 22.5 hours of continuous Bluetooth battery life on the Jabra Evolve3 85, ChatGPT's 'best for work calls' pick. That is behind its 31.75 hours for the Sony WH-1000XM6 and well under Jabra's 'up to 55 hours (with ANC on)' claim, though RTINGS also measured just under 98 hours on the USB dongle.
standout_why: SoundGuys' cited 'best noise canceling headphones for work' page (dated 2026-10-22) gives the Evolve3 85 only Jabra's claimed 'up to 55 hours with ANC on'. It gives no numeric mic scores and lists the Sony at 37 h 14 min in its own test. RTINGS' office list (2026-10-16) gives the Sony 31 h and the Space Q45 about 28 h, and says the Jabra's mic noise handling is 'not quite as robust as the Sony's'. It gives no Jabra battery figure. SoundGuys' conference-calls list (2026-03-24) has no mic or battery numbers for these picks. I could not load the text of the cited RTINGS phone-calls list or of What Hi-Fi, only their titles, so I could not rule out either page holding the figure. RTINGS' numeric mic results (SpNR, noise handling) are locked to members on every review, so no rival shows them either.
decides: This keeps the split ChatGPT gave but adds a cost to the Jabra pick. SoundGuys (Adam Birney) says to pick the Evolve3 85 over the XM6 'if you want better battery life and mic quality'. Yet RTINGS' Bluetooth runtime for the Jabra (22.5 h) is shorter than its Sony XM6 figure (31.75 h), so for phone or Bluetooth use the Sony is the longer-lasting of the two. The Jabra's battery edge only holds on its dongle (just under 98 h per RTINGS), which suits a PC desk worker. For a budget pick, RTINGS says the Space Q45 (27.8 h) has a better mic than the newer Space One Pro (36.1 h), which Dealectric lists. SoundGuys found the Space 2 Pro's mics 'very good', so it is the soundcore model with named mic praise.
